question.text: Famous Tang poet Li Bai was born in a town along this trading route from China to the Mediterranean. A particular Chinese fabric gave this trading route its name.
question.clue: A 2015 best-selling history book by Peter Frankopan is titled for the plural form of this entity.

swap.text: Ulaanbaatar is the capital of this Asian country, the center of a former empire led by Genghis Khan.
swap.clue: The prince Kul Tigin is honored by 7th century inscriptions named for a river valley in this country's west, the Orkhon, which was a power center for the Gokturk state.

question.leadin: Answer some things about the foreign policy of George W. Bush.
question.text: Following the 9/11 attacks, the United States invaded Afghanistan in order to overthrow this political group which controlled the country and harbored Al Qaeda.
question.clue: It was opposed by a contingent of non-Pashtun warlords known as the Northern Alliance.

swap.leadin: As a child, this person defeated their blood brother Jamukha and rescued their kidnapped wife Borte ["BOHR-tay"] from a rival tribe.
swap.text: Name this person, who ruled the largest contiguous empire in history. This person born with the name Temujin was succeeded by their son Ogedei.
swap.clue: This leader adopted the Uyghur script and established the extensive yam postal service.

question.text: The heqin policy was later revived by the Tang when Princess Wencheng ("win-chung") was sent to marry this region's king Songtsen Gampo. A monastery in this Himalayan region's capital of Lhasa was built to house a Buddha statue she supposedly brought.
question.answerHtml: Tibet [or Bod or Xizang; accept Tibetan Empire or Tufan or Tubo]
question.clue: This region's future was settled by a Seventeen Point Plan agreed to by representatives of a man who had been tutored by Heinrich Harrer.

swap.text: This offshoot of the Mongol empire was ruled by Batu, and located in modern-day Russia and eastern Europe. Sometimes called the Kipchak Khanate, legend has that it took its most common name from the color of Batu's tent.
swap.clue: Uzbeg converted it to Islam, less than a century after Batu established it.

question.leadin: Genghis Khan and this man shared a common ancestor, Tumanay Khan.
question.text: Name this conqueror who supposedly killed over five percent of the world population and who built a pyramid of skulls.
question.clue: This man's grandson, the ruler and astronomer Ulugh Beg is buried in the same mausoleum, the Gur-e Amir.

swap.leadin: This ruler forced the Assassins to surrender their fortress at Alamut, and killed hundreds of thousands in his sack of Baghdad.
swap.text: Name this Mongol grandson of Genghis Khan who founded the Ilkhanate. The Mongol advance westward was stopped by his defeat at Ain Jalut by the Mamluks.
swap.clue: Nasir al-Din al-Tusi convinced this ruler to establish an observatory at Maragha.

question.text: This republic on the Yenisey near Mongolia was independent, with its capital at Kyzyl, from 1921 to 1944.
question.clue: Under Chinese rule from 1757 to 1911, Russia helped it achieve independence in 1911 and annexed it in 1944.

swap.leadin: In the 1990s, this country's leader renamed the town of Janga for himself, Kerki for his father, and Yylanly ("yuh-lahn-luh") for his mother.
swap.text: Name this country where doctors were required to follow an oath to its president, Saparmurat Niyazov, instead of the Hippocratic Oath.
swap.clue: The Rukhnama, or "Book of Soul," was a propaganda work written by a former head of this state, Saparmurat Niyazov.

question.text: Batu, a grandson of Genghis Khan, formed this khanate, known for its colorful tents, in a large area that included part of modern Russia.
question.clue: In addition to Egidu, Mamai, and Jani Beg, one of its leaders sacked Moscow in 1382, and was named Tokhtamysh.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the history of a mountainous nation that's been in the news a lot.
swap.text: In 1893, the British set up this border between Afghanistan and Pakistan based on geographical features, not ethnic regions. This idiotic idea continues to lend itself today to ethnic tensions.
swap.clue: The creation of this line, named for a British diplomat, effectively created a buffer zone between Britain and Russia in Asia. This line forms the de facto border between Afghanistan and Pakistan.

question.text: The Ballad of Mulan instead depicts her fighting the Rouran ("roh-rahn"), who are the first historical people of note to use this title for their rulers. This Turkic title was also given to the leader of the Mongols.
question.clue: One of these figures destroyed the Khwarezmian cities of Urgench and Samarkand and established his capital at Karakorum.

swap.leadin: In his 2002 "Trashcanistan" article, Stephen Kotkin argues that this country is the only post-Soviet Central Asian state to not depend on Russia.
swap.text: Name this former Soviet Republic whose leader Rafiq Nishabov was removed by Moscow in 1989 after failing to stop ethnic violence against this country's Meskhetian Turks, which culminated in the Fergana massacre.
swap.answerHtml: Uzbekistan [or Republic of Uzbekistan; accept Oʻzbekiston Respublikasi; accept Uzbek Soviet Socialist Republic or Uzbek SSR or Uzbekskaja Sovetskaja Socialističeskaja Respublika or Oʻzbekiston Sovet Sotsialistik Respublikasi; accept Uzbekia]
swap.clue: In one event in this country, Chulpon Avenue was closed and hundred of people in Bobur Square were killed in a protest blamed on the Islamic group Akramia.

question.leadin: This conflict was partly prompted by one nation's fears that another would stage an invasion of India.
question.text: Give this name for the strategic rivalry for supremacy in Central Asia between Britain and Russia during the late nineteenth century.
question.clue: The Fortress of Orenburg was constructed in order to control the Kazakhs as part of this period, which also saw extended maneuvering over the rights to Sinkiang.

swap.leadin: Of the 16,000-plus men to begin a journey from this city, only assistant surgeon William Brydon survived to reach Jalalabad (juh-LAHL-uh-bad).
swap.text: Name this city from which Lord Elphinstone led a disastrous retreat in 1842. In modern times, the Saur (SAH-wur) Revolution ended after Sardar Daud Khan was assassinated in this capital city.
swap.clue: Leaving from Khanadar, this city was captured by Ahmad Shah Durrani whose son Timur Shah moved the capital of their empire to this city in 1772.

question.text: The author of History of the Hind, al-Biruni, traveled to India with the invading forces of Mahmud-i Zabuli, the first Sultan of this Turkic empire which broke off from the Samanids.
question.answerHtml: the Ghaznavid Empire [or Ghaznaviyan; Mahmud’s father Sabuktigin founded the dynasty but Mahmud was the first to call it a Sultanate]
question.clue: This empire whose first leader, Sabuktigin, was a slave before being promoted by Alptigin.

swap.leadin: A traveler displays his sextant and compass to this city's "Koosh Begee" upon being asked of his scientific prowess in an account by Sir Alexander Burnes.
swap.text: Name this city in Central Asia. The Manghit Dynasty ruled an Emirate named for this city in Transoxiana, which was also the capital of the Samanid Dynasty.
swap.clue: A group modelled off the Young Turks invited the Soviet conquest of this city and was given prominent leadership positions in the short-lived Soviet republic centered on this city.

question.text: In response to Olzhas Suleimenov's "Nevada" movement, Nazarbayev closed this Kazakh nuclear facility in 1991. This facility's namesake city on the Irtysh River suffered from increased birth defects and cancer rates as a result of the 456 nuclear tests conducted there, including the very first Soviet test in 1947. It is also known by a geometric name.

swap.leadin: Members of this ethnicity formed a 300-year confederation with the Cumans, with whom they are sometimes identified.
swap.text: Identify this ethnicity of Baibars and most rulers of the Bahri dynasty.
